@missingOption: shown in an automation's sentence in place of a choice (of a select or status property) or a course that has since been deleted

group.@logic: heading of a section of the formula reference (in the window where a formula is written): functions for conditions, like if() and and()
group.@math: heading of a section of the formula reference: functions for numbers, like round() and sum()
group.@text: heading of a section of the formula reference: functions for text, like lower() and replace() (a noun)

group.@lists: heading of a section of the formula reference: functions for lists of values, like count() and join()

args.@if: What a formula function takes, one phrase per value given to it, separated by commas: shown after its name in the formula reference (“if() · a condition, a value if true, a value if false”). The error that repeats it is its own message (error.takes). This one is for if()
args.if: a condition, a value if true, a value if false
args.@ifs: what ifs() takes (see the note on “if”): pairs of a condition and a value, and a last value for when none is true
args.ifs: conditions and values, then a fallback
args.@conditions: what and() and or() take: any number of conditions (each true or false)
args.@condition: what not() takes: one condition (true or false)
args.@value: what empty() and format() take: any one value
args.@ifEmpty: what ifEmpty() takes: a value, and what to use instead when it's empty
args.@round: what round() takes: the number, and how many digits to keep after the decimal point
args.@number: what floor(), ceil(), abs() and sqrt() take
args.@pow: what pow() takes: a number, and the power to raise it to
args.@mod: what mod() takes: a number, and what to divide it by
args.@numbers: what min(), max(), sum() and average() take: any number of numbers, or lists of them
args.@text: what lower(), upper(), trim(), toNumber() and date() take: a piece of text
args.@texts: what concat() takes: any number of pieces of text
args.contains: text or a list, what to find
args.@contains: what contains() takes: where to look, and what to look for
args.@startsWith: what startsWith() takes: a text, and the beginning to check it for
args.@endsWith: what endsWith() takes: a text, and the ending to check it for
args.replace: text, what to find, what to put instead
args.@slice: what slice() takes: a text, and the positions where the part to keep starts and ends
args.@split: what split() takes: a text, and what to cut it at (like a comma)
args.@repeat: what repeat() takes: a text, and how many times to repeat it
args.@date: what year(), month(), daysUntil() and other date functions take
args.dateAmountUnit: a date, an amount, a unit
args.@dateAmountUnit: what dateAdd() and dateSubtract() take: a date, a number, and a unit like weeks
args.dateBetween: a date, another date, a unit
args.@dateBetween: what dateBetween() takes: two dates, and the unit to count in, like days
args.@formatDate: what formatDate() takes: a date, and a pattern for how to write it (like MMM D)
args.@list: what count(), first(), last(), unique() and sort() take
args.@at: what at() takes: a list, and the position of an item in it
args.@join: what join() takes: a list, and what to put between its items (like a comma)

doc.@ifs: what ifs() does; {example} is a formula using it, kept as written

doc.or: True when any condition is true
doc.not: True when the condition is false

doc.@sum: what sum() does; {example} is a formula using it, kept as written
doc.average: The mean of the numbers given
doc.@toNumber: what toNumber() does; {example} is a formula using it and {result} what it gives, both kept as written

doc.@lower: what lower() does: gives the text in small letters
doc.@upper: what upper() does: gives the text in capital letters
doc.@contains: what contains() does; {example} is a formula using it, kept as written

doc.@split: what split() does; {example} is a formula using it, kept as written

doc.@first: what first() does: gives a list's first item
doc.@last: what last() does: gives a list's last item
doc.at: The item at a position, from 0

doc.@join: what join() does; {example} is a formula using it, kept as written

error.unclosedText: This text is missing its closing quote

takes.if: {fn} takes a condition, a value if true, a value if false
takes.@if: Error when a formula function is given too few or too many values: what it takes, as the reference lists it (see the messages under “args”), as a whole sentence. {fn} is the function's name with () after it, kept as written. This one is for if()

takes.@ifEmpty: error when ifEmpty() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is ifEmpty()
takes.@round: error when round() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is round()

takes.@pow: error when pow() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is pow()
takes.@mod: error when mod() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is mod()
takes.@numbers: error when min(), max(), sum() or average() is given no values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is the function's name
takes.@text: error when lower(), upper(), trim(), toNumber() or date() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is the function's name
takes.@texts: error when concat() is given no values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is concat()
takes.@textOrList: error when length() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is length()
takes.contains: {fn} takes text or a list, what to find
takes.@contains: error when contains() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is contains()
takes.@startsWith: error when startsWith() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is startsWith()
takes.@endsWith: error when endsWith() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is endsWith()
takes.replace: {fn} takes text, what to find, what to put instead
takes.@replace: error when replace() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is replace()
takes.@slice: error when slice() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is slice()
takes.@split: error when split() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is split()
takes.@repeat: error when repeat() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is repeat()
takes.@date: error when year(), month(), daysUntil() or another date function is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is the function's name
takes.dateAmountUnit: {fn} takes a date, an amount, a unit
takes.@dateAmountUnit: error when dateAdd() or dateSubtract() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is the function's name
takes.dateBetween: {fn} takes a date, another date, a unit
takes.@dateBetween: error when dateBetween() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is dateBetween()
takes.@formatDate: error when formatDate() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is formatDate()
takes.@list: error when count(), first(), last(), unique() or sort() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is the function's name
takes.@at: error when at() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is at()
takes.@join: error when join() is given too few or too many values (see the note on “if”); {fn} is join()

example.@daysUntil: example formula: how many days are left until a due date

example.@joinText: example formula: a first name and a last name put together (Join is a verb)

actions.@action: screen-reader name of the menu choosing what an action does (set a property, add a row…), in a button's or an automation's list of actions

type.@set: a choice in that menu: what an action does
type.@add: a choice in that menu: what an action does (adds a row to a database)

watchOption.@date: a property in the menu of what starts an automation (see the note on “title”); {property} is its name, a date property
watchOption.@checkbox: a property in the menu of what starts an automation (see the note on “title”); {property} is its name, a checkbox property
watchOption.@url: a property in the menu of what starts an automation (see the note on “title”); {property} is its name, a property holding a web address
watchOption.@email: a property in the menu of what starts an automation (see the note on “title”); {property} is its name, a property holding an email address
watchOption.@phone: a property in the menu of what starts an automation (see the note on “title”); {property} is its name, a property holding a phone number
watchOption.@course: a property in the menu of what starts an automation (see the note on “title”); {property} is its name, a property holding one of your school courses
watchOption.@relation: a property in the menu of what starts an automation (see the note on “title”); {property} is its name, a property linking to rows of a database
watchOption.@files: a property in the menu of what starts an automation (see the note on “title”); {property} is its name, a property holding files from your library

automations.@changesTo: screen-reader name of the menu that picks which change starts an automation (any change, or a particular value)
automations.@anyChange: choice in that menu, after a property's name
automations.@isChecked: choice in that menu, after a checkbox property's name
automations.@isUnchecked: choice in that menu, after a checkbox property's name
automations.@becomes: choice in that menu, after a property's name; {option} is the name of one of its choices (Done)
automations.empty: No automations yet. For example: when Status becomes Done, set a Finished date to today.
automations.@sentence: an automation as one sentence (“When Status becomes Done, set Finished to today”); {when} is what starts it and {actions} what it does
automations.@thenJoin: joins an automation's actions in its sentence (“set Finished to today, then open the page”); {before} is the actions so far and {next} the next one
automations.@doNothing: the end of an automation's sentence when it has no actions yet (“When a row is added, do nothing yet”), in lowercase because it follows a comma
automations.@whenAdded: the start of an automation's sentence: what starts it
automations.@whenAnyProperty: the start of an automation's sentence, for a property that no longer exists
automations.@whenChanges: the start of an automation's sentence; {property} is a property's name
automations.@whenChecked: the start of an automation's sentence; {property} is a checkbox property's name
automations.@whenUnchecked: the start of an automation's sentence; {property} is a checkbox property's name
automations.@whenBecomes: the start of an automation's sentence; {property} is a property's name and {option} one of its choices (Done)

templates.@newRowFrom: heading of the menu that picks what a new row starts from: an empty row or a template
templates.@emptyRow: choice in that menu: a new row with nothing in it
templates.@default: badge on the choice (an empty row or a template) that new rows start from when none is picked: it's the default one
templates.@emptyRowOptions: screen-reader name of the button with the empty row's options
templates.@defaultForView: menu command: new rows in this view of the database start from this template (or an empty row)
templates.@defaultForEveryView: menu command: new rows in every view of the database start from this template (or an empty row)
templates.@untitled: the name shown for a template that has no title yet
templates.@editNamed: screen-reader name of the button that opens a template to change it; {title} is the template's name
templates.@editUnnamed: screen-reader name of the button that opens a template with no name to change it
templates.@moreNamed: screen-reader name of the button with a template's other commands; {title} is the template's name
templates.@moreUnnamed: screen-reader name of the button with the other commands of a template with no name
templates.@new: button that makes a template: a row that new rows can start from
templates.tip: A template is a row to start from: its values and its page (a checklist, headings, notes) are copied into each new row.
